incidents-bot: PAGER: Multiple NCCL collective failures observed in prod-gpu-pool-7 (rendezvous timeouts, intermittent communicator resets). Auto-escalation -> #incidents.

ada-oncall: I'm awake. Paging into bridge, grabbing recent logs and affected job ids.

ada-oncall: quick customer-impact check: alerting shows ~9% of inference requests in pool-7 returning 500 / timing out over the last 5m. Latency tail spikes to ~3s.

sophia-eng: seeing the same. From node-7b logs: repeated NCCL aborts with "Unrecoverable error: Device or resource busy" then leader flip. Also a burst of Xid 79 entries in dmesg on gpu03.

sophia-eng: snippet: ```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (79): GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679012] kernel: gpu_driver: rmw timeout waiting for ...
[ 12346.000123] inference-container[pid]: NCCL WARN AllReduce timed out, aborting communicator
```

mike-rt: sounds like a transient PCI/NVLink or driver-level glitch triggering NCCL rendezvous mismatch. We should: 1) cordon node gpu03, 2) drain pods gracefully, 3) force fallback to single-GPU model variant for inflight jobs if possible.

ada-oncall: cordoning gpu03 now -> `kubectl cordon gke-prod-gpu03`

incidents-bot: NOTE: automatic retry configured for model-route `text-gen-2` -> will attempt fallback to quantized-v2 when communicator errors detected.

james-mlinfra: rolling the traffic split to fallback variant for the route. command: ```rbac
POST /api/route-splits
{ "route": "text-gen-2", "split": {"quantized-v2": 0.5, "base-v3": 0.5}}```

elaine-sre: draining pods on gpu03, killing misbehaving container ids with repeated NCCL aborts. Using `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=10` for the worst offenders.

ada-oncall: monitoring error rate. After cordon/drain + traffic split, error rate dropped from 9% -> 1.5% over 3 minutes. Latency tail improved but a few stragglers remain.

sophia-eng: interesting: several failures show a rendezvous leader flip during an allreduce window where tensor parallel group size = 4; logs show one rank reported unable to join due to ephemeral netlink timeout. Could be noisy NIC or kernel oom_killer interaction.

mike-rt: can we check kernel oom logs? Also confirm no user pods hitting host OOM. `journalctl -k | grep -i oom`

sophia-eng: ran that — nothing obvious besides the Xid79 lines. Also `nvidia-smi -q` on gpu03 returned ECC errors counts incrementing.

james-mlinfra: for immediate mitigation I'm recommending: 1) keep node cordoned, 2) set rendezvous timeout to be more forgiving for pipelines (reduce false aborts) by increasing NCCL env vars on new pods: `NCCL_TIMEOUT=120000`, `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1`. We'll roll that via a canary first.

ada-oncall: creating a canary deployment with NCCL_TIMEOUT=120000 in us-west-2 prod replica set. Rolling to 10% first.

incidents-bot: UPDATE: customer-facing status page set to "Degraded: Multi-GPU inferencing in us-west affected; fallbacks in place."

elaine-sre: note for postmortem - capture dmesg, nv-driver version, kernel version, and full NCCL logs for all ranks in the job. I've submitted a request to infra to snapshot gpu03 and preserve logs (avoid rebooting).

ada-oncall: handoff to james-mlinfra and sophia-eng for deeper triage. I'm un-assigning oncall at 5401240450.

james-mlinfra: taking next shift. I'll coordinate kernel/driver rollback testing in staging and schedule a graceful evacuation of the rest of the pool if ECC counts keep rising.

sophia-eng: I'll start correlating heaviest workloads with model sharding patterns (tensor vs pipeline) to see if a particular sync pattern exacerbates the issue.

mike-rt: temporary mitigation checklist added to incident runbook: cordon+drain suspected node, enable fallback route, increase NCCL_TIMEOUT on new pods, preserve node logs, open P1 postmortem if >5% sustained error rate or >30m duration.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT HANDOFF: paged -> resolved_partial. Follow-up: oncall postmortem required.

ada-oncall: thanks all. If anything flips back up ping me. :thumbsup:
